proposition_crosswalk.title: Scope versus result
proposition_crosswalk.identical_proposition: Compare semantic rules, required input roles and declared coverage before treating later evidence as a replacement. Generated IDs and equal totals do not establish semantic identity. Reject missing required roles, but do not reject equivalent rules just because generated IDs differ.

proposition_crosswalk.title: Reuse versus fresh proof
proposition_crosswalk.identical_proposition: Saved configuration may be useful when its old result is stale. Reuse the method without copying its passing outcome or live input authority. Preserve unrelated records and verify changes through exports and reopened state.

proposition_crosswalk.title: Coverage versus count
proposition_crosswalk.identical_proposition: After changing a test runner, reconcile exact executed identities, duplicate executions and skipped or omitted tests. A green aggregate or unchanged count does not establish full execution; preserve earlier failed evidence.

proposition_crosswalk.title: Producer versus assumption
proposition_crosswalk.identical_proposition: Inspect the actual producer schema before interpreting output. Structured text, unsupported formats and truncation require different handling. A batch exit code cannot substitute for each relevant component result.

proposition_crosswalk.title: Correction versus annotation
proposition_crosswalk.identical_proposition: Follow a changed fact through the actual consumer decision, persisted state and exported artifact. Changing a label or citation alone does not correct an obsolete calculation or decision.

proposition_crosswalk.title: Applicability limit
proposition_crosswalk.identical_proposition: These lessons describe prior observed corrections, not universal success rules. Use current requirements to decide applicability, retain contradictory evidence and avoid extra reflection when ordinary implementation and checks suffice.
